subject: English
description: Degrees of comparison — positive, comparative, superlative; irregular forms; double comparison; converting between degrees.

questions.stem: Identify the correct comparative form: 'My house is ___ than yours.'
questions.explanation: DEGREES OF COMPARISON — three forms: (1) POSITIVE: BIG (just describes). (2) COMPARATIVE: BIGGER (compares two things; uses '-er' or 'more'). (3) SUPERLATIVE: BIGGEST (compares three+ things; uses '-est' or 'most'). RULES for adding -er/-est vs more/most: (a) ONE-SYLLABLE adjectives: usually -er/-est (big→bigger; tall→taller; small→smaller). (b) TWO-SYLLABLE adjectives ending in -y: change y→i, add -er/-est (happy→happier→happiest; busy→busier→busiest). (c) TWO+ SYLLABLE adjectives: usually 'more'/'most' (beautiful→more beautiful→most beautiful; difficult→more difficult). (d) Some 2-syllable can take EITHER (clever→cleverer/more clever; both correct). DOUBLE COMPARISON ERRORS: 'more bigger' or 'most biggest' — INCORRECT. Use either '-er' OR 'more', not both. SAMPLE GOOD: 'My house is bigger than yours' (compares 2). 'This is the biggest house on the street' (compares 3+). PYQ FREQUENCY: degrees-of-comparison in SSC CGL Tier 1, IBPS Clerk Pre, RRB English 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Pick the correct: 'She is ___ student in the class.'
questions.explanation: Superlative form needs 'THE' before it (most uses): 'THE most intelligent', 'THE tallest', 'THE best'. The phrase identifies a UNIQUE entity in a group, so DEFINITE ARTICLE 'the' is needed. PRACTICE: (1) 'Mt Everest is THE TALLEST mountain in the world.' (2) 'Honesty is THE BEST policy.' (3) 'This is THE OLDEST temple in India.' WHY 'THE': because the SUPERLATIVE PICKS OUT a SPECIFIC item (the unique 'best/tallest/longest one'). EXCEPTIONS — superlative WITHOUT 'the' (more rare): (a) When superlative is used as ADVERB: 'She works hardest of all the team.' (b) Predicative use sometimes: 'She is best when relaxed.' (c) After possessive: 'her best work'. DOUBLE-SUPERLATIVE error: 'She is the most tallest' — WRONG (combine '-est' OR 'most', not both). PRACTICE — IRREGULAR forms (memorize): (1) good → better → best. (2) bad → worse → worst. (3) much/many → more → most. (4) little → less → least. (5) far → farther/further → farthest/furthest. (6) old → older/elder → oldest/eldest. PYQ FREQUENCY: superlative + 'the' in SSC CGL, IBPS English 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Correct sentence: 'No other planet in our solar system is ___ Jupiter.'
questions.explanation: POSITIVE-DEGREE COMPARISON uses 'AS + adjective + AS' to indicate equality. 'No other planet is AS LARGE AS Jupiter' = 'no other matches Jupiter's size' — implies Jupiter is the largest. NEGATIVE FORM: 'NOT AS X AS' or 'NOT SO X AS' (older). PRACTICE: (1) 'My brother is as tall as me' (positive equal). (2) 'Diamond is not as soft as graphite' (positive inequality). EQUIVALENT in COMPARATIVE: 'Jupiter is LARGER THAN any other planet' — same meaning, different degree. EQUIVALENT in SUPERLATIVE: 'Jupiter is THE LARGEST planet (in our solar system)'. KEY DEGREE TRANSFORMATIONS — interchanging: (1) POSITIVE: 'No other X in Y is as ADJ as Z' (e.g., 'No other planet is as large as Jupiter'). (2) COMPARATIVE: 'Z is more ADJ than any other X in Y' or 'Z is more ADJ than all other X' (e.g., 'Jupiter is larger than any other planet'). (3) SUPERLATIVE: 'Z is the most ADJ X in Y' (e.g., 'Jupiter is the largest planet'). EXAM-FAVOURITE TASK: convert from one degree to another preserving meaning. PRACTICE: 'Honesty is the best policy' (superlative) → 'No other policy is as good as honesty' (positive). PYQ FREQUENCY: degree-conversion in SSC CGL, IBPS PO, CAT 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Pick the comparative: 'Of the two friends, Raman is ___ than Suresh.'
questions.explanation: COMPARATIVE DEGREE used when COMPARING EXACTLY TWO entities. 'Of the TWO friends, Raman is RICHER than Suresh.' KEY RULE: with two items, use COMPARATIVE (-er or 'more'); with three+, use SUPERLATIVE (-est or 'most'). EXAMPLES: (1) 'Of the two brothers, Ramesh is the elder.' (NOT 'eldest'.) (2) 'Of three brothers, Ramesh is the eldest.' (NOT 'elder'.) (3) 'She is the better of the two students.' (4) 'She is the best of the three students.' EXAM-FAVOURITE TRAPS: (a) Using superlative for two → WRONG. (b) Using comparative for three+ → also wrong, but less commonly tested. SPECIAL CASES with 'OF THE TWO/THREE': always uses 'THE' even with comparative when 'of the two': 'the better of the two', 'the elder of two brothers'. POSITIVE: comparative for 2 = 'X is bigger than Y'. INCORRECT 'doubly intensive' forms: 'most fastest' (×), 'more better' (×). EXCEPTION — 'most' as 'very': 'most beautiful sunset' could mean 'very beautiful' OR 'the most beautiful' (context-dependent). PYQ FREQUENCY: 'two vs three+' degree usage in SSC CGL, IBPS PO 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Choose: 'The price of gold is increasing day by day. It is becoming ___ '
questions.explanation: 'MORE AND MORE + adjective' = expression of GRADUAL INCREASE / progressive change. 'It is becoming MORE AND MORE expensive' = price is rising continuously. PARALLEL FORMS: (a) 'BIGGER and BIGGER' / 'TALLER and TALLER' (using -er + -er). (b) 'MORE and MORE expensive' (using more + more). (c) 'LESS and LESS' for decreasing. (d) 'WORSE and WORSE' for irregular. PRACTICE: (1) 'The traffic is getting worse and worse every year.' (2) 'She became more and more confident as she practiced.' (3) 'The road grew narrower and narrower.' (4) 'The candidates' speeches were less and less convincing.' RELATED IDIOMATIC EXPRESSION: 'THE + comparative ... THE + comparative' = parallel growth: 'The MORE you study, the BETTER you'll do.' 'The HIGHER you go, the COLDER it gets.' 'The MORE the merrier' (proverbial). RELATED — 'AS + adjective + AS POSSIBLE' = maximum extent: 'as quickly as possible'. EXAM TIP: 'more and more X' is GRAMMATICAL & idiomatic; 'most X' is just superlative. PYQ FREQUENCY: progressive comparatives in IBPS PO Mains, CAT, CGL Tier 2 — 1× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests idiomatic comparative usage.

questions.stem: Identify the correct: 'Mathematics is ___ subject for me than Hindi.'
questions.explanation: 'MORE DIFFICULT' is COMPARATIVE form of 'difficult' (3 syllables — uses 'more'). Sentence compares TWO subjects (Math vs Hindi) → COMPARATIVE. With INDEFINITE article 'A': 'A more difficult subject' (introduces it as ONE OF some difficult subjects, not specific). 'THE more difficult' would be used if it's UNIQUE/specific (e.g., 'the more difficult of the two'). KEY: ONE-SYLLABLE adjectives (-er): big→bigger, fast→faster, tall→taller, smart→smarter. TWO-SYLLABLE -y adjectives: happy→happier, busy→busier, easy→easier (change y→i). TWO-SYLLABLE other: usually 'more' (modern→more modern, careful→more careful). THREE+ SYLLABLE: always 'more' (intelligent→more intelligent, beautiful→more beautiful, ridiculous→more ridiculous). DON'T DOUBLE-COMPARE: 'more difficulter' is WRONG — 'difficult' takes 'more', not '-er' suffix. SAMPLE: 'This problem is more difficult than that one' (correct comparative). 'This is the most difficult problem in the book' (correct superlative). EXAM-FAVOURITE TRAPS: (a) Double comparison/superlative. (b) Wrong inflection for word length. (c) Mistakes in irregular forms (good/bad/much). PYQ FREQUENCY: regular vs irregular comparison in SSC CGL, IBPS PO 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Convert from POSITIVE to COMPARATIVE: 'No other metal is as malleable as gold.'

options.option_text: Gold is more malleable than any other metal
Gold is the most malleable metal here
Gold is malleable like other metals
Gold is as malleable as other metals

questions.explanation: POSITIVE-TO-COMPARATIVE conversion: 'No other X is as ADJ as Y' → 'Y is MORE ADJ than ANY OTHER X'. Plug: 'No other metal is as malleable as gold' → 'GOLD is MORE MALLEABLE THAN ANY OTHER METAL.' Note: 'any other' is KEY — without it, comparison would be illogical (gold is more malleable than gold itself!). KEY TRANSFORMATIONS (memorize for SSC, IBPS): (1) POS: 'No other X is as ADJ as Y' ↔ COMP: 'Y is more ADJ than any other X' ↔ SUP: 'Y is the most ADJ X'. (2) POS: 'Few X are as ADJ as Y' ↔ COMP: 'Y is more ADJ than most X' ↔ SUP: 'Y is one of the most ADJ X'. (3) POS: 'A is as ADJ as B' ↔ COMP: 'A is no less ADJ than B' / 'B is no more ADJ than A'. (4) POS: 'A is not as ADJ as B' ↔ COMP: 'B is more ADJ than A' / 'A is less ADJ than B'. SAMPLE: 'Honesty is the best policy' (sup) → 'No other policy is as good as honesty' (pos) → 'Honesty is better than any other policy' (comp). EXAM IMPORTANT: in conversions, use 'ANY OTHER' (not 'any') to avoid logical contradictions. PYQ FREQUENCY: degree conversions in SSC CGL Tier 2 grammar, IBPS PO Mains 1-2× per paper.
